title: Convert Sorted List to Binary Search Tree
summary: Given a singly linked list with elements sorted in ascending order, transform it into a height-balanced binary search tree.
statement: Given a singly linked list with elements sorted in ascending order, transform it into a height-balanced binary search tree.
constraints: 0–20000 linked-list nodes in nondecreasing order, with values from -100000 to 100000; repeated values are allowed.

Return a TreeNode root (None for an empty list). Its inorder values must equal the complete input list, including duplicates, and every subtree must be height-balanced. Tree shape need not match the example.
reference_solution:
def sorted_list_bst(head):
    length, current = 0, head
    while current is not None:
        length += 1
        current = current.next
    current = head
    def build(count):
        nonlocal current
        if count == 0:
            return None
        left_count = count // 2
        left = build(left_count)
        root = TreeNode(current.val)
        current = current.next
        root.left = left
        root.right = build(count - left_count - 1)
        return root
    return build(length)
target_space_complexity: O(log(n+1)) auxiliary recursion, plus O(n) returned nodes
hints: A linked list cannot access its middle by index cheaply, but its order is already the desired inorder traversal.
Count the nodes, build a left subtree of a chosen size, consume the current list node as root, then build the right subtree.
Keep one advancing list cursor. build(count) recursively creates count//2 left nodes, consumes one cursor value, and creates the remaining right nodes.
The cursor advances only after the left subtree is built. Duplicate values still represent separate required tree nodes.
editorial: First count the list length. Recursive subtree sizes determine a balanced shape, while a shared list cursor fills the nodes in inorder, advancing exactly once per input node. This takes O(n) time without copying the list into an auxiliary array. New TreeNode objects are required: ListNode objects are the input, not the returned tree. The independent oracle fills inorder positions of a complete heap-indexed tree from the original JSON values. Grading allows any balanced shape, checks every duplicate occurrence, and uses iterative checks so an incorrect deep chain is rejected without a checker recursion overflow.

tests.explanation: One valid tree has root 5, left subtree containing -10,-3,0, and right child 9. Other balanced shapes with the same inorder values are equally correct.
An empty linked list becomes an empty tree: return None, displayed as [].
